name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 10 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Johnny Olszewski holds a massive fundraising edge, over $1 million raised versus roughly $20,000 for Dave Wallace
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 94% to win
No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, leaving fundamentals as the main evidence
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Olszewski: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly 50-to-1, with markets agreeing the seat is safely Democratic. With no polling to refine the estimate, the expected margin stays near the low twenties.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a competitive race, or significant outside spending against Olszewski, would be the first sign this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District sits in the Baltimore suburbs and leans Democratic by about ten points, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is running for reelection. His Republican challenger, Dave Wallace, has raised only about $20,000 and reports just over $3,000 on hand, while Olszewski has raised more than $1 million and holds over $600,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democrat around 94 percent. Everything points to a comfortable Olszewski win, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the outcome.
